text: The rwb-integration service runs as one login created with the rwb_integration schema by the platform DB work (DP-02); the story names it "the rwb-integration login" until the name is agreed.
why: No source gives the login name, and every DP-02 row requires one login per service; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery service identity.
read: RWB-P2-E2002-APP sections 3, 10 and 13; DP-02 in Template and Rules section R5.5; Architecture v5 slide 41 (one schema and one login per service).
confirm: ACE DB owner and the platform DB story, before the rwb_integration baseline is created
impact: None on behaviour: the login is named by role in the story and swapped for the agreed name without a content change.

text: The plan is read through the ACE common module's published RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor interface with a 2,000 ms budget per call and batches of 500 account numbers, and not through recovery.v_ace_plan; rwb_integration holds no grant on recovery. The interface is a module interface (INT-34) and not a view, so the direct call of the legacy story stays where the legacy story has it.
why: The Technical Specification reads v_ace_plan with a fallback, while ADR-010, DP-05 and Architecture v5 slide 45 give the thirty views to rwb-source-data alone; the legacy story calls the published interface, and the interface is the only path that keeps a plan engine fact out of the view contract.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 12 (RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor) and section 4 step 3; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 and T-A.2 API-P2-010; Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 13, 29, 37, 41 and 45; ADR-010; DP-05 in Template and Rules section R5.5.
confirm: Solution architect and the ACE team at the wave 2 contract review, with the rwb-source-data owner
impact: If the read moves behind rwb-source-data, this story's client and the contract of RWB-P2-E2002-CON change and the batch and budget move to that contract; the answer and the behaviour do not change.

text: The answer of this service is live from ACE on every 200 that read ACE: live is true, the plan fields are the ones ACE returned or absent when it returned no plan, and messageCode is empty. The flag-off answer is 200 with live false and no plan. live false with MSG-P2-008 and the stored date is the rwb-case stored answer on its own base. The composite route takes the live answer when it has one and the stored answer otherwise.
why: The legacy resource carries live and messageCode and answers the stored value from the same endpoint; the split into two providers leaves the flag as the only way for a caller to tell a live value from a stored one, and no source states which provider fills the message.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 12 (PlanStatus with live false when not live from ACE) and section 5 X2 (the view shows the stored status); API Specification v4 PlanStatus; RWB-P3-E2002-APP AC5 and section 15 (the stored answer carries live false and MSG-P2-008 with its date); DP-19 in Template and Rules section R5.5.
confirm: Case owner (RWB-P3-E2002-APP) and the edge owner (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) at the contract review
impact: If the message moves to this service, the stored date has to be passed to it or read from the case, and the field's rule changes; the flag and the answer shape do not.

text: The RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor answer is taken as a list of plans, one per plan, each carrying planRef, accountNo, status and statusDate for the account numbers asked, and an account with no plan is absent from the list rather than answered as an error or as a null element.
why: The legacy story publishes the four element names and not the null rules, the empty answer or the error of the interface, and the difference between an absent plan and an error decides whether the case side keeps or clears its stored value.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 12 (List<PlanStatusView> RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor(List<String> accountNos); // planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate) and section 5 X1; RWB-P2-E2002-CON section 12.2.
confirm: The ACE team at the interface review of RWB-P2-E2002-CON
impact: If the interface answers an error for an unknown account, the client maps it to a no-plan answer; the answer shape and the criteria do not change.

text: The account numbers of the case are read through the rwb-case case read by case reference, with the owner and queue, before the ACE call; the authorise answer is taken as a grant of Case record R with the case in or out of scope. The case read and the authorise call are consumed as published contracts and this key holds no copy of a case row or an account row.
why: The operation is case-scoped and takes the case reference only, the ACE interface is keyed by account number, and the rights check needs the owner and queue; no source fixes the read, and the work package's contract row names only three rwb-case contracts.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 2 (the cases with their account numbers through the P3 CaseQuery) and section 12 (GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status, request: path caseId); RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 4 step 3; API Specification v4 x-capability Case record R; DP-11 in Template and Rules section R5.5.
confirm: Case owner (the rwb-case contract baseline) and the access owner at the contract review
impact: If the caller passes the account numbers instead, the client loses one hop and the path keeps a query parameter; the behaviour does not change.

text: The batch size of 500 and the timeout of 2000 ms are read at run time as parameter rows of rwb-case through its parameters contract with the version in force, never as code; a change of the version is picked up without a redeploy, and the deployment carries the same two names as its defaults.
why: The legacy story records both as service properties and marks them assumed under DL11, while DP-06 makes parameters and their versions rwb-case data; a value in code would break the guardrail that no business value sits in code.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 3 and section 13 (rwb.ace.plan.batch-size = 500 and rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms = 2000, assumed; DL11); DP-06 in Template and Rules section R5.5; Ownership Map parameter_catalog and parameter_value owner P3; RWB-P2-E2002-CON section 12.2.
confirm: The parameters owner (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) and the ACE team at the contract review
impact: The two values may change without a release; if they stay deployment values, the read is the values file and no behaviour changes.

text: The plan-status answer is taken as planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate, live and messageCode, with the legacy PlanStatus field set and accountNo added; the plan-reference, account-number and status-date types are the legacy ones (a reference up to thirty characters, an account code, a date), and the contract names the fields and leaves lengths and null rules to the review with the owners.
why: The API Specification fixes five field names and no accountNo, the legacy interface answer carries the account, and the sibling case story joins on it; a contract cannot be faked without deciding whether the field is in the answer.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 12 (PlanStatus: planRef, status, statusDate, live, messageCode; RestructurePlanQuery returning accountNo); API Specification v4 PlanStatus; RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 12.2 (the answer carries planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate, live).
confirm: Solution architect and the case owner at the contract review
impact: If the field is removed, the case side joins on the plan reference it already receives; no business value changes.

text: The consumed reads are taken as follows: the case read answers the case reference, its account numbers, the owner, the queue and the closed flag; the reference read answers the LOV-PLAN-STATUS rows with the version in force; the parameter read answers the two setting rows with the version in force; the authorise answer grants or refuses Case record R and says whether the case is in the caller's scope. Each is one hop with a 2 s budget, and none is declared as provided by this service.
why: The paths and element names of the four reads are given nowhere, and the fakes cannot be written without them; the owners are fixed by the Ownership Map and the dependencies by DP-06, DP-07 and DP-11.
read: Ownership Map v1 (recovery_case, case_account, reference_row, reference_version, parameter_catalog, parameter_value owner P3; the authorise path owner P4); DP-06, DP-07 and DP-11 in Template and Rules section R5.5; RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 12.2.
confirm: The rwb-case contract owner (RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON) and the rwb-access owner at the contract review
impact: A renamed element touches one client and one fake; no behaviour changes.

text: live and messageCode are taken as follows: live is true on every 200 answer that read the ACE common module, and false on the flag-off answer, which reads nothing and carries no plan; messageCode is empty on every answer of this service, because it holds no stored value and has no older date to name; live false with MSG-P2-008 and the stored date is the rwb-case answer on its own base, and the composite route prefers the live answer when it has one.
why: Both fields exist in the API Specification and neither has a rule; the split into two providers makes the flag the only way to tell a live value from a stored one, and the message has a date that only the case side holds.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 12 (live is true when read from ACE now) and section 5 X2; API Specification v4 PlanStatus; RWB-P3-E2002-APP AC5 and section 12.1; DP-19 in Template and Rules section R5.5.
applied_in: 7 AC1 and AC3; 8 Business rules BR4; 12.1; 12.8
confirm: The edge owner (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and the case owner at the contract review
impact: If the message moves to this service, the stored date has to be passed in or read from the case; the flag and the shape do not change.

text: The interface is taken as follows: RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor receives a list of account numbers and answers a list of plans, each with planRef, accountNo, status and statusDate, in batches of 500 with a 2000 ms budget per call, a breaker per downstream and one retry of a read with jitter; an account with no plan is absent from the list, an interface failure is an error and not an empty answer, and an answer larger than the batch is split and merged by account.
why: The legacy story publishes the signature and four names and nothing about batching, null rules, error classes or the empty answer; the Technical Specification instead reads a view, which ADR-010 and DP-05 refuse, so the interface contract has to be written down here.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 3 (batches of 500, assumed; DL11), section 5 X1 and section 12; TSD P2 v3 T-A.2 API-P2-010; Arch v5 slide 45 and ADR-010; DP-05 and DP-11 in Template and Rules section R5.5; RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG section 12.5.
applied_in: 7 AC2 and AC6; 8 Business rules BR7; 12.2; 12.5; 13
confirm: The ACE team at the interface review of RWB-P2-E2002-CON
impact: If the interface answers one plan per call, the client loops and the batch value has no effect; the answer and the criteria do not change.

text: The composite route for the case record is taken as one edge answer that calls rwb-integration and rwb-case in parallel, one hop each, prefers the live answer when live is true, and otherwise shows the stored answer with MSG-P2-008 and its date; the route path and its merge order are the edge contract's and are not fixed here.
why: The legacy screen was served by the monolith; the split gives the plan section two providers, and no source fixes the route path or the merge, so a readable default is recorded rather than invented in code.
read: Arch v5 slides 10 and 12 (the BFF composes a few parallel calls, one hop each, and merges at the BFF); DP-19 in Template and Rules section R5.5; RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 15.
confirm: The edge and gateway owner (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) with the screen design
impact: The route and the merge may change; the two provider answers and their fields do not.

text: The deployment values are taken as follows: the worker runs as the rwb-integration identity carried as a secret reference; the ACE endpoint, its certificate reference, the breaker values, the replica counts, the resource sizes, the probe timings, the alert thresholds and the log level are values files of each environment; the release creates no Schedule and no workflow and applies no migration; and the schema step proves that the login holds no grant on recovery or on another rwb_ schema.
why: DP-02 requires one login per service and gives no name, the platform rule gives the namespace and the queue and no endpoint, and the plan read is an outside call that every environment has to point somewhere; the no-Schedule and no-migration statements are the two release checks the split makes necessary.
read: Arch v5 slides 11, 16, 20, 24, 41 and 44; Temporal and Drools design slides 11 and 27; Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-02, DP-10 and DP-15; Ownership Map interface_config and job_catalog (P2).
applied_in: 8 Business rules BR1, BR3, BR4 and BR5; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.7; 13 Solution plan
confirm: DevOps lead, the ACE DB owner and the platform administrator at the release readiness review
impact: No business value changes; the values are tuning and environment data, and a release that adds a table or a Schedule is refused.

text: The trigger wiring is taken as follows: the plan-status step of DailyCaseRun and its readPlanStatus activity are rwb-case's and call the operation one case per call with the case reference only and a 2 s client budget; gateway-bff calls it for the case record and merges it with the stored answer of rwb-case; this service creates no Schedule and registers no workflow or activity for the key; and the release records per environment whether the ACE answer comes from the published endpoint or from the contract stub.
why: The sibling story and the job map agree that the daily step is rwb-case's, the integration harness lists a step on rwb-integration, and no source states how an environment is flagged when ACE is not yet reachable; without the record an environment can believe it reads ACE when it reads a stub.
read: Arch v5 slide 44 (JOB-02 owner rwb-case, mechanism AceDataReady to DailyCaseRun) and slide 13 (no P3 to P2 cell); RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 4 step 3 and section 12.5; RWB-P2-E2002-CON section 12.5; DP-10 and DP-11 in Template and Rules section R5.5.
applied_in: 7 AC4; 8 Business rules BR3 and BR11; 11 Data; 12.5; 12.6
confirm: Case owner (RWB-P3-E2002-APP), the edge owner and the ACE team at the release readiness review
impact: If the step is ever moved to this service, a Schedule and a workflow are added and the alert set changes; the read and its answer do not.

text: The observability is taken as follows: the five series are live answers, no-plan answers, unknown status codes, unavailable and refused answers by class, and call duration against the budget, each with the environment, the release and the build ID as dimensions; four alerts are wired, three carrying MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 and one the unknown status code and its count, each with one runbook entry; a fifth mapping row names the no-package-in-force refusal with its owners and no wiring. The four runbook entries are ACE unavailable, unknown status code, refused caller, and stored fallback with the no-package routing. The synthetic fixtures of the smoke run are owned by the DevOps team of the release and are created in DEV and SIT only.
why: ADR-023 requires observability per service, the message catalogue requires a message identifier per alert, and no source lists the series, the thresholds, the runbook entries or the fixture owner; the five series follow the answer states the app story declares, and the fourth alert carries no message because the legacy story gives none for an unknown code.
read: ADR-023; Template and Rules section R7.2 s14; Arch v5 slides 33, 42 and 44; legacy RWB-E2-002 section 5 X3 (message None) and section 14; RWB-P2-E2002-CON section 14 and RWB-P2-E2002-APP section 14.
applied_in: 7 AC5 and AC6; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
confirm: DevOps lead, the on-call rota and the platform administrator at the release readiness review
impact: Every alert an operator receives has one message identifier and one runbook entry, no dashboard or alert exposes personal data, and no alert claims a condition this service cannot see.
